expect_nodes.note: positive control: the Go chi server (GET and POST /users collapse into route:/users). Measured present, so a missing ENDPOINT is a client gap, not a broken fixture

expect_edges.note: routing proof: HttpStackResolver pairs the clj-http GET to chi r.Get("/users")
routing proof: the clj-http POST pairs to chi r.Post("/users")

forbid.note: exactly GET and POST /users; the (str base "/users") call in user-count may join GET /users but must not mint a third

forbid.name: HEAD /users
forbid.note: MEASURED VIOLATED: scan_clojure_routes' reitit branch sees `[r (client/get (str base "/users") {:headers ...})` as route data and `block.contains(":head")` matches `:headers`, minting a phantom client-side ROUTE. ROUTE is not an http_client kind, so this does not cap the cell; it is the precision record for the clojure route scanner

note: clj-http, the dominant Clojure HTTP client (hato shares its (client/get url opts) call shape). server/main.go is a Go chi server exposing GET and POST /users, so a failing cell isolates to the Clojure client. user-count is the idiomatic base-URL form with an auth header; it is not asserted as an ENDPOINT (a dynamic (str base ...) URL) but it is the source of the HEAD /users phantom above. BASELINE (0.4.18 wheel, HEAD 8155f47): the Clojure parser emits no ENDPOINT at all, so the cell is `none`. The route control and both HTTP_CALLS pairings were verified satisfiable against this exact server dir with a python requests client (2/2 HTTP_CALLS, 2/2 ENDPOINT_HIT).
